topic.angle: How compounding frequency changes the real yearly rate

body.question: A deposit pays a 4.65% rate, compounded monthly. What annual percentage yield (APY) would the bank quote?
body.reveal: About 4.75%. APY restates a rate as if it compounded over one year, so the interest that is added each month and then earns interest of its own is counted. That makes APY a fair way to compare accounts that compound on different schedules, although it does not account for account fees.

probes.question: True or false: APY takes account fees into account.
Why is a monthly-compounded 4.65% rate worth 4.75% a year?
options: Interest added during the year earns interest too

claims.claim: APY restates a rate on a one-year compounding basis
claims.quote: is a normalized representation of an interest rate, based on a compounding period of one year

claims.claim: APY is a fair way to compare accounts with different compounding schedules
claims.quote: APY figures allow a reasonable, single-point comparison of different offerings with varying compounding schedules.

claims.claim: APY does not account for fees (probe 1 false)
claims.quote: it does not account for the possibility of account fees affecting the net gain

claims.claim: Interest added during the year earns interest too (probe 2)
claims.quote: Compound interest or anatocism is interest accumulated from a principal sum and previously accumulated interest.
